title: The Li–Li undirected multiple-unicast conjecture
formal: For every finite undirected network with positive rational edge capacities and independent unicast sessions, is the zero-error causal network-coding rate region, under the entropy-capacity convention below, equal to its fractional multicommodity-routing region?
definitions: Let G=(V,E) be a finite connected undirected graph, with capacities c_e>0, and let (s_i,t_i), i=1,…,k, be ordered pairs of distinct vertices. Different pairs may share endpoints. Source s_i initially knows its own message M_i, uniformly distributed over a finite alphabet; the messages are mutually independent. A finite deterministic code specifies in advance a finite sequence of directed edge uses. Each transmitted symbol is a function of messages initially at its sender and symbols previously received there. Every t_i must recover M_i for every message tuple. Local computation and storage are unrestricted; nonlinear functions are permitted. Let X_{u→v} be the whole tuple sent from u to v on edge {u,v}, and measure Shannon entropy H in bits. For a scale b>0, the code supports r∈R_{≥0}^k when H(M_i)≥b r_i for all i and H(X_{u→v})+H(X_{v→u})≤b c_{uv} for every edge. Define C(G) as the closure in R^k of all such supported rate vectors, over all finite alphabets, codes and scales. This explicitly fixes the entropy formulation used in the cited network-coding literature, with exact decoding and capacity shared between directions; it is not a definition using two independent full-capacity arcs. Define R(G) by nonnegative real path flows f_{i,P}, for simple s_i-to-t_i paths P, satisfying Σ_P f_{i,P}≥r_i and Σ_{i,P:e∈P} f_{i,P}≤c_e. The target is C(G)=R(G) for every G and session list. No multicast destinations, correlated sources, initial side information about other messages, or computation of functions in place of message recovery is supplied.
answer_criterion: Prove C(G)⊆R(G) for every specified network and session list; the reverse inclusion follows by routing and closure. Alternatively, exhibit a finite undirected instance with a coding-supported rate vector outside the closed routing polytope, together with a valid causal code and a proof of fractional-routing infeasibility. The latter can use a linear-programming dual certificate. Beating integral edge-disjoint paths, a particular routing algorithm, or a cut bound that is already larger than the routing optimum is insufficient. A multicast or directed-network advantage does not refute this unicast conjecture. A theorem about vanishing-error codes must be related explicitly to this zero-error entropy formulation.
context:
Routing treats each message as a separate commodity that consumes capacity along paths. Network coding lets an intermediate node combine messages before forwarding them. If a node knows bits x and y, it may send x⊕y; a receiver that already knows y can recover x. Whether the necessary side information can be supplied cheaply enough to improve total throughput depends on the entire network. The conjecture says that undirected edges always let fractional routing match the best coding rate for independent one-destination messages.

Fractional routing is essential to the comparison. A message may be split among many paths, and different commodities may share an edge up to its total capacity. This is more flexible than requiring one path per message or requiring edge-disjoint paths. The rate region is described by a linear program, so an apparent coding improvement over a greedy routing choice does not establish a gap. One must beat the optimum over all fractional routings.

The capacity convention also matters. An undirected edge of capacity one has one combined budget for both directions, rather than a separate budget of one in each direction. The formal statement follows the cited entropy-based definition: the entropy of each complete directional transcript is counted, and decoding is exact. Taking the closure permits limiting rates. This states precisely which capacity notion is being compared instead of assuming that all zero-error, fixed-length and vanishing-error conventions are interchangeable.

Cut constraints provide a necessary upper bound: information needed across a partition must cross its boundary. For multiple commodities, satisfying every cut constraint need not make the demands fractionally routable. Jain, Vazirani, Yeung and Yuval study the small K_{3,2} example with four same-side sessions. Its sparsity bound is one, while its maximum concurrent routing rate is 3/4; their entropy inequalities show that coding also cannot exceed 3/4. The gap between cuts and flows therefore does not by itself give a coding advantage.

Braverman, Garg and Schvartzman show that a counterexample would have consequences well beyond one small network. Any fixed coding advantage greater than one can be amplified into a family with a gap growing as a positive power of log |V|. A general logarithmic upper bound comes from multicommodity-flow and cut relationships. Thus even a modest strict separation would open the door to much larger asymptotic gains.

The conjecture is also connected to computation rather than communication alone. Afshani, Freksen, Kamma and Larsen show that it implies an Ω(n log n) lower bound for constant-degree Boolean circuits multiplying two n-bit integers. Their reduction turns a sufficiently small circuit into a forbidden network-coding advantage. This is a conditional circuit lower bound, not an already proved consequence of ordinary cut arguments.

Recent positive results remain sensitive to the session arrangement. Vamsi and Thakor’s ISIT 2025 work handles specified asymmetric demands in layered networks, including partition-symmetric demands in their Type-I bipartite family. It also studies gaps between routing constructions and information-theoretic bounds for three-layer cases. Such a gap is a reason to examine an instance more closely; it is not itself a demonstrated coding scheme outside the routing region.

An August 2026 preprint by Liu, Que, Li and Li reports new cases via graph metrics, including networks with at most five terminal locations and certain planar instances supported on at most three designated face boundaries. In the planar case, each session has both endpoints on one of those faces. Five terminal locations is not the same restriction as five sessions or five total graph vertices. The general conjecture remains explicitly open in that paper.

The strongest recent undirected separation located in this review changes the demand model. Braverman and He obtain a superconstant multicast coding advantage using locally decodable codes. Each source message there must reach a set of receivers, and the routing comparison is a Steiner-tree packing problem. Replacing those copies by independent unicast messages removes exactly the shared-message structure used by the construction, so the result does not disprove Li–Li.
why: Asks whether computation inside an undirected network can increase the throughput of independent unicast messages, with direct connections to multicommodity flow and major computational lower bounds.

importance.reason: A central capacity conjecture whose resolution would clarify the power of network coding and influence circuit and data-structure lower bounds.

progress.text: Li and Li formulate the undirected no-coding-advantage conjecture, as recorded in the subsequent primary literature.
Jain and coauthors prove that the four-session K_{3,2} example has coding rate equal to routing rate 3/4.
Braverman–Garg–Schvartzman show that any constant strict advantage amplifies to a polylogarithmically growing gap.
Afshani and coauthors derive conditional multiplication-circuit lower bounds from the conjecture.
Vamsi–Thakor analyze specified asymmetric demands in layered networks.
Braverman–He give superconstant undirected multicast gaps; the unicast conjecture is explicitly left open.
Liu–Que–Li–Li report metric-based proofs for further network classes, including at most five terminal locations.

A separate session-interaction framework reduces the conjecture to a property of all irreducible cores; it does not establish that property universally. Its manuscript corrects a quantifier in the conference definition to require one common witnessing solution.

status_note: The August 2026 primary papers explicitly leave the general conjecture unresolved. This card fixes causal zero-error coding with entropy capacities and closure of rates, as in the cited formal model. Restricted topology results, multicast gains and alternative error conventions are distinguished. Review cutoff: 11 September 2026.
